# Programming Fundamentals

::: {.callout-note}
This page covers the basics of programming using examples in both R and Python. Each of the codeblocks below is **interactive**. You can edit the code and rerun it to see how the results change. We encourage you to play around to build your understanding
:::

## Basics 

The most common way you will interact with Python and R is through a **REPL** (read-evaluate-print-loop):

- You type out one or more statements (instructions)
- You ask the language *interpreter* to *execute* (evaluate) 
- It returns (prints) any output 
- Repeat

Try changing the statement below and rerun the code to see what happens:

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

## R

```{webr}
# This is a comment R will ignore
# Try changing the statement below and rerun the code to see what happens
1 + 1
```

## Python

```{pyodide}
# This is a comment Python will ignore
# Try changing the statement below and rerun the code to see what happens
1 + 1
```

:::

## Values, variables, and types

To do more than simple calculations we need to *store* inputs and outputs (**values**). To do this we declare **variables** which can store different **types** of values:

### Text

To store text as a variable we use single `''` or double `""` quotes to create a **string**: 

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

## R

```{webr}
# We assign variables use <-
a_string <- "hello psyc 201"

# Typing a variable by itself prints out its value
a_string
```

## Python

```{pyodide}
# We assign variables using =
my_string = "hello psyc 201"

# Typing a variable by itself prints out its value
my_string
```

:::

### Numbers

We typically work with two kinds of numbers: *integers* (round numbers) and *floats* (contain decimals):

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

## R

```{webr}

```

## Python

```{pyodide}
# Integers
my_number = 3
my_number
```

```{pyodide}
# Floats
my_decimal = 3.1
my_decimal
```

:::

### Comparisons

This allows us to compare values:

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

## R

```{webr}

```

## Python

```{pyodide}
# We can make comparisons
my_decimal > my_number
```

```{pyodide}
# Not equal
my_decimal != my_number
```

```{pyodide}
# We can intuitively combine comparisons with `and`
my_number > 2 and my_number < 10
```

```{pyodide}
# Using `or`
my_number > 0 or my_number < 1000
```

```{pyodide}
#| error: true
# What happens here?
my_number > my_string
```

:::
